nodes.label: Gas Camera Daytime Flock Frame (2022-02-23 11:00:32)
nodes.description: Colour overhead still from the '1080P-IPC-Gas' channel at 2022-02-23 11:00:32. Birds are noticeably smaller and paler than in the March frames, consistent with an earlier point in the grow-out cycle. A horizontal feed pipe crosses mid-frame with four red-topped pan feeders; birds form tight rosettes around each pan while the lower third of the floor is nearly empty. Feed is visibly present in the pans.

nodes.label: 1080P-IPC-Gas Camera Channel
nodes.description: Camera channel labelled '1080P-IPC-Gas', viewing a feeder line almost perpendicular to the lens axis so the pipe runs left-to-right across the middle of the frame. Appears in both the February and March frames of this chunk, providing a fixed viewpoint across which bird growth can be compared.

nodes.label: Suspended Pan Feeder Line
nodes.description: The dominant fixed structure in every frame: a horizontal feed-conveyor pipe carrying evenly spaced circular pan feeders with red conical tops and white grill spokes. Because the pans are rigidly spaced and never move, they act as natural spatial anchors and as regions of interest for scoring feeding behaviour and feeder occupancy.
nodes.rationale: Anchoring behaviour analysis to the feeder line is attractive because the equipment geometry is constant across all cameras and dates, so feeder-zone occupancy can be counted without any per-frame calibration; the red pan tops also give a strong colour cue for automatic localisation in the daylight/colour frames.

nodes.label: Early Grow-Out Stage (Small Birds, Late February)
nodes.description: In the 22-27 February frames each bird occupies a small fraction of the pan-feeder diameter, and large areas of bare floor remain visible between birds. This gives a low apparent stocking density and well-separated individual blobs, which is the easiest regime for individual detection and tracking.
